title: S-Bounded Short-Message Tradeoffs for Randomized Modes
summary: Birthday-length one-query distinguishers defeat the between-query-state formulation, but they do not settle the corresponding tradeoff bounds in the short-message regime.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether $S$-boundedness can prove tradeoff bounds of order $O(\sqrt{Spq/N})$ in the short-message regime $p\ll\sqrt{N}$ for randomized $\mathrm{CTR}\$ instantiated with a permutation and for randomized $\mathrm{OFB}\$, $\mathrm{CBC}\$, and $\mathrm{CFB}\$, analogous to the positive bound for $\mathrm{CTR}\$ instantiated with a pseudorandom function. Birthday-length, one-query distinguishers at $p=\Theta(\sqrt{N})$ defeat the between-query-state formulation in that regime but do not rule out such bounds when $p\ll\sqrt{N}$. Here $S$ is the memory or state bound, $p$ is the message-length parameter, $q$ is the query parameter, and $N$ is the block-domain size.

scope.domain: Symmetric-encryption security and time-memory tradeoffs for randomized block-cipher modes, including permutation-based CTR and randomized OFB, CBC, and CFB.
assumptions: The adversary is subject to S-boundedness.
The short-message condition p is much smaller than the square root of N applies.
parameters: S, the memory or state bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether S-boundedness can establish tradeoff bounds of order O(sqrt(Spq/N)) for the listed randomized modes in the short-message regime p much smaller than sqrt(N).

citations.label: Tight Time-Memory Trade-Offs for Symmetric Encryption

progress.summary: The source presents the target as a possible S-boundedness proof direction for randomized CTR with a permutation and randomized OFB, CBC, and CFB. It records birthday-length one-query distinguishers at the birthday scale, while stating that these do not rule out the shorter-message tradeoffs.
citation_labels: Joseph Jaeger et al., Tight Time-Memory Trade-Offs for Symmetric Encryption
